answer: Agents selling walnut crop maps or relic surveys through a beacon service could require a fresh fee burned for each earning key every epoch. Validators check a burn receipt bound to that key and epoch, reject reuse, and exclude keys without one. Each added alias permanently pays another fee, even in a parallel farm; set it above the expected extra identity subsidy. This assumes enforceable burns and realistic reward estimates. Wealthy farms can still pay, and honest newcomers face the same recurring entry cost.
